created_by: Dylan L.R. Pollock with Atlas continuity support
description: Master Plan v120.1 realigns the project around the current prototype-to-polished Huey Brain V1 path. The custom Intel Core i9-12900K system is the active prototype and primary operator workstation, while the polished Huey Brain V1 and Huey Body are being built and are not yet operational. The Lenovo Legion Go and ASUS FX505DT are LabTech. Briefcase is HueyTech. HIMS is merged append-only infrastructure without controlling authority, PyHuey is the primary external prototype cockpit, Huey Body actuation proceeds as a bounded parallel track, and Huey Farm remains funding-dependent with an approximately 80 GB pooled-VRAM testing goal.

current_session_evidence: Generated-artifact cleanup merged into main via PR #743.
Salvaged local work was protected and later merged via PR #745, reducing the broad WIP surface to eight changed files before merge.
Legacy root compatibility wrappers were removed via PR #746, leaving canonical implementations under src/huey/memory/PY and src/huey/media.
Media-tool consolidation merged through PR #747, centralizing audio analysis under huey.media while retaining huey.audio compatibility.
HIMS foundation merged through PR #748 with src/huey/messaging, HIMSMessage, HIMSEvent, HIMSStore, tests, and architecture documentation; it is not wired as a controlling runtime.
The 2017 iMac 5K was decommissioned; reusable RAM was moved into the ASUS FX505DT.
The custom i9-12900K system is the active prototype Huey Brain development platform and current primary operator workstation, not the polished Huey Brain V1.
The Lenovo Legion Go is Windows 11 LabTech for feature testing; the ASUS FX505DT is Debian Forky mobile LabTech.
Briefcase is HueyTech: an LTE-capable portable field terminal intended to maintain reachability/liveness checks and support document work.
PyHuey is active both as a standalone application and embedded connector, and is the primary external prototype cockpit.

Command Center repository inspection found a runnable AI-generated React/Vite GUI prototype with mock-first data, stale metadata, incomplete integration, and credential-handling concerns; it is not operational infrastructure.

current_reality.summary: The project is developing the fixture-to-log proof on a custom i9-12900K prototype Huey Brain platform, then transferring and reproducing it on a polished Huey Brain V1. The polished Huey Brain V1 and Huey Body are active builds but not operational. LabTech supports development and feature testing. Briefcase is portable HueyTech. HIMS is merged append-only infrastructure without runtime authority. Huey Body actuation is a bounded parallel track, and Huey Farm awaits funding.
current_reality.active_proof_loop: known MP3 fixture -> FFmpeg/media preparation -> local transcription -> response bridge -> structured JSON/JSONL log
current_reality.current_phase: Prototype Huey Brain development, fixture-to-log proof validation, polished Huey Brain V1 build, and parallel Huey Body work
active_truths: The custom i9-12900K system is the active prototype/development platform and current primary operator workstation; it informs but is not identical to the polished Huey Brain V1.
The polished Huey Brain V1 and Huey Body are being built and are not yet operational.
The fixture-to-log proof is developed and validated on the prototype, then must be reproduced on polished Huey Brain V1.
Huey Body actuation may advance in a bounded parallel track but cannot become a dependency of the cognitive proof.
LabTech enters, prepares, observes, archives, and recovers; it does not become Huey.
HueyTech includes explicitly classified Huey-side builds, portable systems, software, and infrastructure; each capability retains its own operational status and authority boundary.
Temporary-use devices and cloud/editor tools may support work but do not become canonically sovereign components.
HIMS doctrine and append-only foundation are merged infrastructure, not a full routing or controlling authority.
PyHuey is the primary external prototype cockpit and exists both as a standalone application and embedded connector; it is not Huey sovereignty or a proof-loop dependency.
Command Center is an experimental AI-generated GUI sandbox, not trusted operational infrastructure.
explicit_non_claims: No live microphone is active in V1.
No wake word is active in V1.
No Huey Body actuation is required for fixture-to-log V1 completion.
No full HIMS/ThunderMail runtime governs V1.
No multi-agent constitutional governance is active in V1.
No Huey Farm compute is part of V1.
No claim is made that polished Huey Brain V1 or Huey Body is operational.

hims.name: Huey Internal Messaging System

current_implementation_posture.important_boundary: The HIMS package can exist before HIMS becomes a controlling runtime. V1 remains simple pipeline plus structured log.

hims.core_idea: HIMS is the internal message, route, validation, and record layer that lets Huey subsystems communicate without direct memory sharing or hidden authority collapse.
why_it_exists: To make requests, proposals, reports, alerts, refusals, and execution records visible and replayable.
To separate sender, router, validator, executor, and logger roles.
To prevent GUI, portal, LabTech, or agent layers from becoming hidden authorities.
To provide future lawful routing from input to decision to action without bypassing review.

thundermail_relation.ThunderMail: mail-style delivery semantics inside HIMS: inboxes, outboxes, acknowledgements, routing, and queues
thundermail_relation.HIMS: larger trust, validation, routing, compartmentalization, and preserved-record doctrine
thundermail_relation.rule: ThunderMail is delivery behavior; HIMS is the governing internal message system.

HIMSEvent.rule: State changes are separate append-only events.

HIMSStore.role: local JSONL store with send, inbox, outbox, channel, mark_delivered, mark_read, archive, events_for, status_for
HIMSStore.rule: No hidden mutation of previous records.

expansion_plan.name: V1.5 shadow trace
deliverables: non-controlling trace messages for fixture stages
cross-links between run logs and HIMS messages

expansion_plan.name: PyHuey visibility and optional dashboard export
deliverables: bounded read-only inbox/outbox summaries in PyHuey
optional non-sensitive export for experimental dashboards

trust_classes_v120.2_operator_visible: Messages intended for bounded operator/PyHuey visibility.
trust_classes_v120.3_private_or_role_restricted: Bounded agent, role, or office traffic not globally visible.
trust_classes_v120.4_official_record: Messages that become official project/runtime state records.
trust_classes_v120.5_safety_critical: Thermal, power, storage, motion, recovery, or preservation traffic.

v1_boundary: HIMS may be present as a library but not required for V1 completion.
V1 structured run log remains canonical proof artifact.
No citizen mailboxes, governance votes, or action authority in V1.
V1.5 may mirror stage traces to HIMS as shadow messages.
safety_rules: HIMS does not grant authority simply because a message exists.
GUI or LabTech-originated messages must remain bounded and auditable.
No physical action is triggered from HIMS without a separate explicitly authorized, bounded, and auditable execution path.
